They are massive, bumbling humanoids with brutish limbs and wiry blonde hair. They may spawn with a large tree trunk in their hand. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coins|0star=20-29|1star=40-58|2star=80-100}} {{drop row|item=Troll hide|0star=5|1star=10|2star=20}} {{drop row|item=Troll trophy|0star=50%|1star=50%| 2star=50%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Black Forest]] |limit=1|frequency=1|stars=After 2000 meters from the world center}} {{spawn row|type=Possible [[Spawn points|spawn point]] outside [[Troll Cave]]s in [[Black Forest]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=Possible [[Spawn points|spawn point]] inside [[Troll Cave]]s in [[Black Forest]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=During "The ground is shaking" [[Events|event]] after defeating [[The Elder]]|limit=2|frequency=6|stars=Yes, if a [[Love Potion]] is active. Otherwise, No.}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Troll Black Forest]]|limit=2|frequency=667|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == Trolls come in two variants: 1/3rd of Trolls are equipped with a log, while the others are unarmed. Unarmed Trolls have three attacks. === Punch === Leans back before swinging to attack the player in a 5-meter 45-degree horizontal arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 4 seconds when within 4 meters of a player. === Ground slam === Lifts both fists up before slamming them down into the ground (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This slam reaches 4.5 meters out in a 90-degree vertical arc, and can be used every 20 seconds when within 5 meters of a player. This effectively means that the Troll will punch five times before doing a slam, assuming that the player is always in range. When the slam hits anything, including the ground, it also creates a 3-meter area that deals 50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 50 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. This area damage is the same at every star level. === Throw === Throws a large boulder at players within 8–20 meters (50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 60 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The boulder travels at an initial velocity of 15 meters per second and can travel for 4 seconds before disappearing. It has a spread of 10–20 degrees. This has a cooldown of 10 seconds and can be disabled by standing close to the Troll. Log Trolls have two attacks. === Log swing (vertical) === Slams their log into the ground extending out 9 meters and spanning across 90 degrees (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. === Log swing (horizontal) === Swings their log from the side, creating a 10-meter 50-degree arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. ==Strategy== {{For|strategies for defeating Trolls|Aggressive creature strategies#Troll}} * Among the largest enemies in ''Valheim'', Trolls have a physical strength that reflects their size. Ranged attacks with a Bow or Spear are best and kiting a Troll through dense areas of the forest is very effective, as they have large hitboxes that hinder their pathfinding. * Trolls employ massive yet slow attacks that are easy to avoid but very hard to block and parry. Using a [[Bone Tower Shield]] is effective at blocking most of its attacks, provided the player has sufficient health. ** "Pulling" the attention of a Troll and brandishing a tower shield while other players fire arrow volleys is an effective strategy. * Trolls will sometimes fall into deep ditches or pits, or more often, the large pit at a copper dig site. Their poor pathfinding often renders them stuck. ** If a Troll approaches a ditch that is sufficiently deep (at least 6 meters) and does not fall in, it will not willingly walk in. Unable to reach the player, it will stand still, glowering into the pit. After a few moments, it will turn its aggression towards any player structures it can reach. ** Alternatively, if the positions are reversed, standing atop the ledge of a pit allows for easy dispatch with arrows and spears. * Trolls can spawn with or without a tree trunk in their hand. A Troll equipped with a tree trunk has decidedly better range and destructive power than one that is not. == Notes == * A 1-star Troll has a pale green tint, and a 2-star Troll is tinted a ruddy red. * They are tall (7 meters) and can move along corridors 2 meters and wider. * The curative pollen ejected by [[Greydwarf Shaman]]s also heals Trolls, as they share a [[Factions|Faction]]. * They cannot jump or swim, but they will walk along the bottom of shallow water, sometimes getting a considerable distance from the shore. They can walk through shallow water faster than a player can swim. * All the Troll's attacks (except its rock throw) have a [[Damage#Terrain_damage|tool tier]] of 2, which allows players to use Trolls to harvest resources they are otherwise unable to attain at their current equipment level. Trolls are capable of knocking down and breaking apart [[Oak]] and [[Birch]] trees with their attacks, which is especially useful in the early game for obtaining [[Finewood]] without a [[Bronze Axe]] (or better). Trolls can also break [[Copper Deposit|Copper]] and [[Tin Deposit]]s (even with their rock throw attacks), which can allow the player to get [[Bronze]] before killing the first boss, [[Eikthyr]]. ** Additionally, Trolls lured into more hostile biomes will aggressively attack most creatures in that biome, due to them having different Factions. While Trolls are not such a good match for stronger enemies, such as [[Plains]] creatures, they are capable of destroying large numbers of [[Swamp]] creatures, leaving loot like [[Entrails]] and [[Bloodbag]]s in their wake for the player to collect * The [[Love Potion]] increases Troll spawn rate, star chances and alerts them. == Gallery == Valheim Mountain-Troll-2 ver0-79-10.jpg|Mountain Troll preparing to smash a Viking in Deep Forest Troll in-game.png Screenshot 2021-05-18 9.27.56 AM.png|Recently updated Troll visuals Trollinswamp.jpg|Infuriated Troll lashing out at enemies in swamp (new model) File:1 star troll.png|A 1-star Troll at night. File:Helpless.jpg|A Troll trapped and helpless in a defensive ditch. == Trivia == * In Old Norse sources, Trolls were assimilated to Jötnar, the giants from Norse mythology. Only in later Scandinavian folklore did they appear as separate beings. * During the alpha, Trolls in the Black Forest had brown skin covered by green moss, while Trolls in the Mountains had blue skin.https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-903.0-903.13 * The trophy of the brown Troll from the alpha build can be spawned with the command "spawn TrophyForestTroll", and the current troll trophy with "spawn TrophyFrostTroll" * The alpha build Troll trophy can be placed on an [[Item Stand]], however, it is invisible. == Lore == {{Quote|The trolls of Midgard may be fading from your memory, as indeed they are from all the race of man. Few and forlorn, they crouch in damp caves and gnaw on the bones of the weak and foolhardy. The will of Odin has pushed them back into the dark places. But in Valheim they have flourished. It has been centuries since any in Midgard saw the great Trolls stamp flat the land and bring down the trees for joy. Look upon this great and noble sight, wanderers in a strange land! Then take to your heels and run...|[[Runestone]]}} == References == {{Creatures}} [[ru:Тролль]] [[uk:Троль]] [[fr:Troll]] [[cs:Troll]] [[de:Troll]]

[[File:Building screenshot.jpg|thumb|A player building a house]] {{Quote|Raise your own viking mead halls, houses, castles, and more with our powerful construction interface. From knarrs to imposing warships, build legendary vessels to conquer the seas and discover new lands.https://www.valheimgame.com/home/#anchor2}} Valheim features an extensive '''building''' system that can be utilized to design structures to meet the demands of any discriminating warrior. In addition to humble homes and outposts, players also use this building interface to make enormous bases, elaborate works of art, defenses against the [[Creatures]] of Valheim, and unique tools to aid in their survival. Starting out with simple wooden building components, players will eventually gain access to the ability to create stronger structures with various materials, including stone and metal. == Basics == You can build using a [[Hammer]] within the working area of a [[Workbench]]. * Press [1-8] to select the hammer in the hotbar slot * Press [RMB] to open the build menu * Press [Q/E] to switch [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] category * Press [LMB] to chose [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]], and place it * Press [Middle Mouse Button] to remove [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Scroll the mouse to rotate the [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Hold [Shift] to temporarily disable snapping * Hold [Shift] then [Middle Mouse Button] to select [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you are looking at. There are various crafting stations required to be nearby to place certain [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. These include the following: * The [[Workbench]], required to place most [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you have unlocked from the beginning or early on, and some late [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. The Workbench is immediately available and costs 10 ordinary wood to build. * The [[Forge]], required to place most building parts containing metals. The Forge requires [[copper]] to build, and becomes available once the player can mine and refine [[Copper Ore]]. * The [[Stonecutter]], required to place building parts created out of stone, such as the stone walls some abandoned buildings are made out of. The Stonecutter requires [[iron]] to build, and becomes available once the player can collect and refine [[Scrap Iron]]. * The [[Artisan Table]], required to build some crafting stations that as of Patch 0.142.6 are at the end of implemented progression. The Artisan Table requires [[Dragon Tear|Dragon Tears]] to build, which must be obtained by defeating the fourth boss, [[Moder]] the dragon. == Snap building == Most building components can snap to each other. This allows for quick and easy building, but can be temporarily disabled by holding the appropriate key or button. By default, this is L-Shift on mouse and keyboard, and LT+LB on controller. == Structural integrity == {{Main|Building stability}} If there is not enough support, the building pieces will fall down. You may reinforce the building with walls, beams, and poles. When you move the cursor to the building piece, it shows a color range from blue, to green, to red. Blue indicates that the part is as stable as it can be, as dictated by its material. The closer to red on the spectrum, the less stable the part. Attempting to place additional pieces onto one that is fully red may result in the new part breaking off and dropping the resources used to construct it unless the new part has lower stability requirements. The stability of an individual building piece is determined by its material, the stability of the piece it's anchored to and its position relative to it, each additional piece inheriting a fraction of the previous piece's stability. A directly vertical pole of [[Wood]] or [[Stone]] can rise 16 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Wood Wall]], [[Wood Wall Half]], [[Stone Wall 1x1]], [[Stone Wall 2x1]], [[Stone Wall 4x2]], [[Wood Pole 1 m]], [[Wood Pole 2 m]], [[Stone Pillar]]. A directly vertical pole of [[Corewood]] Logs can rise 24 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Log Pole 4 m]] and [[Log Pole 2 m]]. A directly vertical [[Wood Iron Pole]] can rise up to 50 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. Trees, including those planted by the player, will effectively function as "the ground" for support purposes, allowing for extremely high construction. [[File:Structure integrity.png|thumb|Found on [https://www.reddit.com/r/valheim/comments/lqsxki/updated_psa_structural_support_details/ Reddit /Valheim], thanks to [https://www.reddit.com/user/ToddGeorgeKelly/ user/ToddGeorgeKelly/]]] In order to keep tall structures stable, the tallest point should be reinforced by supports that create the shortest and most vertical path possible down to the ground. It is worth considering raising the terrain as much as possible below a structure, such that the floor and walls are 100% stable (highlighted in blue when moused over). Boulders are also considered terrain when calculating stability, so parts that intersect them are considered grounded. == Decay == If wooden building sections are not covered during rain, are not linked to a roof, or are submerged in water, they will decay to a maximum of 50% durability and will seem rotting until fixed. When exposed to rain, defensive structures do not rot decay. Stone, black marble, and crystal structures will not decay when wet or submerged. Building the desired structure's roof first, with the appropriate supports and foundation in place, will aid with constructions lasting days or weeks if rain is a worry. == Damage == Player, monster, and creature attacks can all damage structures. Defensive structures will also receive minor damage while causing harm to creatures that come into contact with them. Aggressive creatures are drawn to and hostile toward all light sources (excluding Jack-o-turnips) and crafting stations, and will try to break them if not attacking a player. == Repair == You can repair building parts that seem to be decaying or damaged with a [[Hammer]]. This does not cost any resources, but does consume stamina. The player must be in range of a crafting station that corresponds to the part being repaired, e.g. a [[Workbench]] when repairing a wooden part, or a [[Stonecutter]] for a stone part. == Abandoned buildings == These structures are a type of [[point of interest]] that can be found to naturally occur in the world. The size, layout, and materials these structures are made of can vary greatly as each is generated from random templates. There are different types of abandoned structures such as Abandoned Cabins, Abandoned Towers, Abandoned Farms just to name a few. These abandoned and generated structures can contain things such as chests with items specific to the biome, monsters (usually [[Skeleton]]s), [[:Category:Creature spawner|monster spawner]]s, and [[wikipedia:Vegvísir|Vegvisir]]s to mark the nearest boss altar for that biome. In the Meadows/Black Forest biome, they can also contain naturally spawning [[Beehive]]s, which will drop a [[Queen Bee]] and sometimes [[Honey]] when destroyed. Players should approach abandoned villages with caution since some villages have been reoccupied by [[Draugr]] and [[Draugr Elite]] who will attack the player on sight. These [[Draugr village|Draugr Villages]] can be identified by partial walls of sharp logs and the buzzing of the [[Creature spawner|spawners]] inside several of the buildings as well as a general miasma and the presence of Draugr both inside and outside the structures. They almost always have a large Mead Hall building that cannot be found anywhere else. There may also be a sentry in a tower armed with a bow who will snipe anything that comes near. == Player base and blocking spawning == {{Main|Player base}} Building certain structures considered to be 'player base' will have the following effects in a radius around them: * Prevent [[creatures|creature]] spawning * Prevent items dropped on the ground from despawning after 1 hour (unless submerged) * Enable player base [[events]] to occur For a full list of player base structures, see [[player base]]. == Base building strategies == [[File:Mordheim server - Guild Castle.jpg|thumb|850x850px]] * Building your outposts in close proximity to '''several biome borders''' grants access to varied resources and allows you to observe the territorial in-fighting of different creatures (complete with loot strewn across the terrain), but can also be dangerous. * Many types of '''defenses''' are possible, both in the form of built objects and altered terrain: ** Creatures cannot dig through terrain, making '''"terrain walls" effectively impenetrable''' to them. Thus the perfect defense is built either with a hoe and a pile of rocks, any pickaxe or ideally a combination of the two. Be warned that terrain alterations may cause stutter just as placing objects does (press F2 to check the number of "instances" loaded). ** A hoe can be used to raise terrain while you're standing on it, allowing you to quickly erect a '''pillar''' to stand on and shoot melee enemies below. Beware that you need a workbench nearby to do this. With practice this is possible during combat. ** Most creatures never jump down from ledges (Fenring and Blobs are exceptions). A '''deep pit''' (around 3 "blocks") is also largely safe, and you can shoot enemies coming close to the ledge. Flying creatures may attack from above if you don't build a roof, however. ** Gates can be destroyed, but '''gaps''' the player jumps over when entering or exiting the base cannot. This trick can be inconvenient, however. Also note that you can '''scale steep terrain''' walls by sprinting and jump-spamming, especially when moving towards a crease (corner) for better traction, while most creatures cannot. ** The most '''FPS-efficient method of defense''' is to build on a few terrain pillars. This minimizes terrain alteration "instances" yet allows you to ignore enemies running around outside, especially if the base entrance requires a quick hop to get on. Note that returning terrain to its roughly native height doesn't remove the FPS hit (unless a true "undo terrain changes" tool is added to the game). ** Workbenches (and campfires) '''disallow enemy spawns''' in their radius, making them surprisingly useful defensive tools. You can hide these in the outer perimeter of your walls or in small pits covered with a few floor tiles to make an area safer. Workbenches also stop dropped items from de-spawning over time, however. ** Doors and gates can be used to create a '''toggle-able bridge''' for carts. Another option to defend your bridge is to hang a gate from a support above it and attach the floor piece to the gate with small gaps on the sides, causing the floor to disappear if the gate is destroyed. ** You can place '''gates in the water''' to block enemies, who will be unable to attack the gates, yet allow boats to pass when opened. * The '''"Level Ground"''' option for the hoe uses the terrain height directly underneath you as the target altitude, though if you hold Shift while clicking it'll use the altitude of the terrain you're pointing at instead. Using this knowledge well may save you a lot of stone and work while landscaping as it only expends stamina and hoe durability. * You can also build a '''"gangplank"''' for enemies to walk on, above your pit base, and put a campfire on it so they'll kill themselves, then catch the loot when it drops down. * Combining a moat with a plateau-based outpost is an interesting option. They are large canines with long, bushy tails that can be bred and [[Taming|tamed]]. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Wolf fang|0star=40%| 1star=2 (80%)| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf meat|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf pelt|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf trophy| 0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}}}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the daytime|limit=3|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=6|stars=Yes|frequency=5}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=4, within 10 meters|frequency=-|stars=Inherited from the parent}} {{spawn row|type=During "You are being hunted" [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=6|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Wolf Mountain]]|limit=8|frequency=4|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating wolves|Aggressive creature strategies#Wolf}} === Attack === This attack has three variations, each with its own 5-second cooldown: a left-swinging bite, a right-swinging bite, and a lunging bite (70 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). In practice, this means that Wolves will typically attack three times in a quick succession before retreating for a moment. These attacks extend 2 meters out in a 60.1-degree horizontal arc and can be used within 2 meters of a player. ==Taming== ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming|Taming.]]'' Wolves can make for powerful allies, both when following a player and when roaming around the built structures. Nighttime Wolves try to despawn during the day, so the taming of starred Wolves must be started during the night. Tamed Wolves will not retaliate against players when they or other Wolves are attacked/killed. A Wolf attacked by a player will be frightened, running around the nearby area for a few seconds before returning to their normal state. Once the taming has started, they will no longer try to flee and will also eat during the day. Taming a Wolf takes 30 minutes, if given enough food. == Breeding == Wolves can breed provided the Wolf is happy and well-fed with [[Boar Meat]] or other raw meat except wolf meat, seeker meat, and bear meat, and there is another Wolf within 3 meters, and no more than 4 Wolves within 10 meters. Once these requirements are met, the Wolf will accumulate love points with each other until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy will last a minimum of 1 minute, after which the birth of the baby Wolf is random chance. Once born, the baby Wolf will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. == Gallery == Wolf1.jpg Wolf2.jpg 1a.png|Comparison of 0, 1 and 2-star Wolves. ==Notes== *A wolf's size is affected by its star ranking. A 2-star Wolf is significantly larger than a 0-star Wolf. *Wolves can be transferred by boat by building a dock with a plank directly over the boat's deck. Wolves don't like to use staircases, so make it as flat as possible. Once the Wolf is over the boat, break the planks it is standing on to load the Wolf onto it. *Wolves will try to fight [[Serpent|Serpents]]. *Wolves will take collision damage if placed on top of the boat. Collision can occur from fish, rocks, and other unknown entities. The collision can occur at any time regardless of the boat's speed; and when it does, it will instantly kill the Wolf. This also occurs with Boars. *When roaming around an area where enemies drop meat, Wolves can not only sustain their numbers but multiply at an alarming rate. This has the advantage of keeping an area highly safe, though overpopulation can become a problem (running into players/carts, attacking structures, stutter on lower end systems, noise). *Tamed Wolves that are set to follow a player will remain where they are when the player logs out or portals beyond their detection range, regardless of the duration of the player's absence. Furthermore, tamed Wolves will resume following the player when they portal/log back in, without needing to manually set them to follow again. *Like (most/all?) creatures, Wolves have infinite stamina and will happily swim across an ocean if you sail slow enough for them to follow you. *Wolves can stand firm on steeper slopes than you can. You can use tame Wolves to your advantage when scaling steep cliffs, as you can lean on them while recovering stamina. However, in other circumstances, their eagerness to approach may nudge you into a tight corner or even off of a precipice. *When being raided by Wolves, it is not necessary to be near a structure for a raid to occur, unlike most raids. *2 Star Wolves can destroy stone structures == Lore == {{Quote|There are friends in Valheim but you must seek them amongst your enemies. Old friends, fire-kin, moon-singers. For centuries they have hunted alongside you, now you must remind them of the old covenant between your people and theirs. Flesh is their delight and must be your offering.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[fr:Loup]] [[cs:Vlk]] [[ru:Волк]] [[de:Wolf]]

He is a [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]] trader wearing a brown cloak, a gold belt and cape. At his camp, Haldor sells several unique items that can be purchased if the buyer has a sufficient amount of [[Coins]] and world progression. ==Biography== Nothing is known about Haldor beyond his occupation as a trader within [[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]. At some point in time, he set up camp within the Black Forest and tamed a [[Lox]] named [[Halstein]] that can be seen feeding from a bowl in the same camp. Haldor is a Dvergr or "dwarf", according to his introduction on Iron Gate's bloghttps://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-713.0-713.40, and how he refers to himself by one of his many quotes. Haldor says multiple phrases including "I'm short for a dwarf", "Check this stuff out", "Take a look at my wares" and "Radjdadaj…" [[Hildir]], Haldor's sister, can be found in [[Meadows]]. ==Location== [[File:HaldorsCamp.png|thumb|right|300px]] Haldor has 10 possible spawn locations that are located in [[Black Forest]]s which are at least 1500 meters away from the center of the world. Approaching any of these locations will permanently place Haldor there. This can happen from 320 to 453 meters away (about twice of the default minimap range) when the related [[Zones]] are generated. When discovered, his bag icon will appear on the world map. He spawns with his own [[Points of Interest (POI)|point of interest]], a small camp consisting of a large wooden wagon pulled by [[Halstein]], a propped up canopy, barrels, tables and multiple display items including spears, swords, shields, helmets and food. The camp is surrounded by a shimmering, transparent dome that acts as a safety zone that [[Creatures]] cannot enter. The safe zone cannot be destroyed. The [[Bearskin Rug]] situated next to Haldor can be destroyed to drop a [[Bear Trophy]]. '''Bonemass''' is the third [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a gigantic humanoid mass comprised of toxic ooze, mud and skeletal remains, likely absorbed from nearby tombs situated close to his altar.

== Summoning ==
[[File:BonemassAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Bonemass' Forsaken Altar.]]
Bonemass' [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Swamp]]s. His location can be found when visiting [[Sunken Crypts]] and sometimes ruined structures, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map.

He is summoned by placing 10 {{Item Link|Withered Bone}}s in his Forsaken altar in Swamps. Like all bosses, Bonemass can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Bonemass|Boss strategies#Bonemass}}
Bonemass has an environment aura that forces raining, which means pulling him from the area cannot be used to remove [[Wet Effect|Wet]].

=== Area of effect ===
Bonemass will charge up with a thick green cloud before vomiting a wave of poisonous ooze, inflicting the [[Poison]] status on everything in a 9-meter radius around him (130 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage). This is signaled when he leans backwards. The poison cloud persists for 15 seconds and will continuously refresh the poison duration on any player that stays inside. This effect cannot be dodged or blocked. Bonemass can use this ability when a player is within 15 meters, and it has a cooldown of 30 seconds. The cloud is centered on the impact point of Bonemass's vomit; due to the size of his collision box, this results in the cloud not reaching very far behind him which gives players a safe area to retreat to that is still within range to strike him.

=== Punch ===
A close-range swipe at a player dealing up to 80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 50 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage to players, in addition to 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage to any trees or rocks hit. This attack can be used every 7 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. It hits in a horizontal 8.5-meter 66.1-degree arc in front of Bonemass.

=== Throw ===
At 50-second intervals, Bonemass will reach into his armpit to throw out a glob of goop in the general direction of the player at an initial velocity of 20 meters per second with a spread of 5–20 degrees. On impact, this ability will attempt to spawn four random monsters ([[Skeleton]]s and/or [[Blob]]s, with equal chances for both). A maximum of eight summons of each type can be active at once; but the selection of enemies each spawning instance is still random regardless of the status of spawn caps, meaning reaching the spawn cap for one type of summon will not force spawns for the other. Bonemass will still attempt to summon creatures even if both spawn caps are reached. This ability can only be used when a player is within 30 meters.

== Aftermath ==
Defeating Bonemass provides the player with a Wishbone, which allows the player to easily locate [[Silver Vein]]s beneath the surface of [[Mountain]] biomes (as well as buried [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in Swamp biomes, and other miscellaneous buried treasures in certain locations).

=== Forsaken power ===
Mounting Bonemass' trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds:

* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Blunt
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Slash
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Pierce
* Block stamina usage: -100%
* Block stamina return: +5

See [[Forsaken_power#Bonemass Power|Bonemass' power]] for more details.

=== Events ===
Defeating Bonemass affects the following [[events]] for that world:

* Disables: Draugr and Skeleton "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: Blobs and Oozers "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: "A skeleton surprise!"
* Enables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." (if [[Moder]] has not been defeated)
* Enables: "There's a smell of sulfur in the air." (if a [[Surtling]] has died)
* Enables: "You are being hunted."
* Enables: "You stirred the cauldron." (if a [[Bat]] has died)
* Enables: "You feel a chill down your spine..."
Note: Two of these events unlock flying enemies that will be uninhibited by base walls and will attack tame animals. For example, bats will quickly wipe out any outdoor tame Boars (if the player has them), most likely before the player can swat them all. Therefore, in order to protect any rare animals (such as a 2-star [[Boar]]), it is advisable to build a secure indoor barn area before undertaking Bonemass.

=== Creature spawning ===
Defeating Bonemass unlocks [[Skeleton]]s to spawn at night in the Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp (additional), Mountain and Plains. They can only have 0 stars.

== Growing behavior ==
Cut forests do not regrow, and naturally occurring small trees (large saplings labelled Beech, Fir, or Pine) do not grow into full sized trees.  Some have reported trees spontaneously appearing on rare occasions, but this will not replace a cut forest (and is quite rare).

It is, however, possible to plant tree saplings using the [[Cultivator]] and [[:Category:Seeds|seeds]] from some tree species. Planted saplings grow into large trees over time. A sapling will grow into a tree after a random passage of time, between 3,000 and 8,000 seconds (between 50 minutes and 2 hours 13 minutes 20 seconds, or about 1.67–4.44 in-game days). Keep in mind that some trees have a shorter maximum growth time and some have a longer minimum growth time.  For tree farms, it is recommended that you plant each sapling 4 meters apart in order to avoid overcrowding, which will eliminate some saplings as surrounding trees mature.  Spacing can be measured by placing poles along one edge of the farm for reference, with the spacing measured by temporarily placing two 2-meter beams.

Ancient trees, Yggdrasil shoots and Scorched Trees do not produce seeds and cannot be planted with the cultivator.

'''Crafting''' is the process of converting and combining [[materials]] to create new [[items]]. 

Some basic items can be crafted in the player inventory, but most items require a dedicated crafting station such as a [[Workbench]] or [[Forge]]. Most gear can also be upgraded to a higher quality, increasing its durability and other aspects.

== Crafting mechanics ==
[[File:Crafting-a-Cultivator.jpg|thumb|The crafting interface of a level 2 Forge, showing the recipe of a [[Cultivator]]. The station level is shown within the star in the top right. The craft tab allows crafting new items, whereas the upgrade tab allows upgrading gear currently in the inventory.]]

Crafting an item at a crafting station requires having the appropriate materials in the [[inventory]], as well as an available slot in the inventory for the result.

Gear that has durability can be repaired for free using the hammer icon at the side of the crafting interface at the crafting station where it was crafted (excluding the inventory). Gear that requires a higher station level to be crafed can also only be repaired at a station at that level, upgrading it does not increase this requirement.

Most weapons, tools and armors can be upgraded to higher qualities, often up to 3 times to a quality of 4. Each upgrade level requires a higher station level. Upgrading increases the durability of the item, and also improves its properties: weapons deal higher damage, while armors provide more [[Armor]]. Upgrading costs a considerable amount of resources and can double or triple the crafting cost of a given item over its cost at quality 1.

For example, the [[Troll Leather Tunic]] requires a level 2 Workbench to be crafted. Thus, it cannot be repaired at a level 1 Workbench. Upgrading it to quality 2 requires a level 3 Workbench, to quality 3 a level 4 Workbench, etc. It initially costs 6 [[Troll Hide]] to craft, but upgrading it to quality 4 costs an additional 11 Troll Hide for a total of 17.

'''Wisp Fountains''' are [[Player base|base]] structures used for collecting [[Wisp]]s, which will be attracted to the fountain when it is dark; either when it is night, or raining, in any biome. Torches and other artificial light sources do not prevent it from summoning wisps.  

They require a [[Stonecutter]] to be built.

== Notes ==
Wisps begin to appear around 18:00. They also appear when it is raining.

A new wisp will join the fountain every 30 seconds, with initially up to three wisps present at a time. Eventually, up to nine wisps can be present near morning.

Hovering over the fountain whilst it is dark enough to attract wisps, it will say, "The wisps are coming." Once the fountain has three wisps, the text will change to "The wisps are dancing." This seems to indicate the fountain has the maximum number of wisps circling it, but it is possible to have more, seemingly due to a bug or quirk in the way the wisp spawning works.

If the player has more than one fountain nearby, the maximum number of wisps is shared among them. Spread the fountains out by more than 20 meters to allow each to reach its maximum.

If they are not caught before the day comes, wisps will fly away and disappear. During the day, while hovering over the fountain, it will say, "The wisps demand darkness."

== Tips ==
* Wisps can also appear during the day if rainy or stormy weather conditions are active. Some players have observed that weather effects triggered by certain boss encounters (such as Eikthyr’s storm) can temporarily allow wisps to spawn even outside normal nighttime conditions, as long as the player remains within the affected area.

* Keeping strong wind active through weather events can also be useful for nearby wind-powered structures, such as windmills, allowing both wisp farming and production benefits at the same time.

* Because wisps will despawn once daylight returns and darkness conditions are no longer met, staying close to the source of the weather effect is required to maintain their appearance.

* In addition to nighttime, some biomes such as the Swamp provide permanent low-light environments, provided the area remains loaded by nearby players.

The '''Wisplight''' is an accessory made of [[Silver]] and [[Wisp]] at a [[Workbench]]. It is unlocked after acquiring a [[Wisp]] for the first time.

==Usage==
The light clears the [[Mist]] of [[Mistlands]] in a 15 meter radius around itself. The orb loosely follows the player and can briefly leave the player in a fog if they change direction too quickly.

It is equipped in the accessory slot, and thus allows players to wear a full set of armor in addition to the light. The Wisplight conflicts with the [[Megingjord]] and the [[Wishbone]], which occupy the same equipment slot.

==Notes==
*When equipped, the message "You release the bound wisp" will appear.
*The mist is also cleared by [[Wisp Torch]]es, the [[Mistwalker]], and some [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]] structures.
**Using the Mistwalker to clear the mist allows you to temporarily wear the Megingjord to transport [[Scrap Iron|Iron]] and [[Copper Scrap]]. Its range is much less than the Wisplight, so this tactic should not be used unless the extra carry weight is needed.

== Trivia ==
* Before the [[1.0]] update, the Wisplight used to clear the mist in only a 10 meter radius.

'''Chain lightning''' is an on-hit effect triggered by weapons upgraded with [[Iolite]] or [[Thunderblood Essence]].

==Effect==
Chain lightning has a 25% chance to trigger on a normal attack and a 20% chance to trigger on a secondary attack.

It deals 75 [[lightning]] damage to the target, the amount is not affected by skills, and it cannot be blocked or dodged.

Once triggered, it has an 80% chance of bouncing off nearby enemies or players. If so, each nearby target within 8 meters has a 30% chance of being targeted, up to a maximum of 2–4 targets per bounce (the maximum is chosen at random then targets are processed starting from the nearest). The process repeats indefinitely, centered on each new target, but with the chance of rebound multiplied by 0.75 each time (i.e., 80% → 60% → 45% → 33.75%, etc.).

A single activation of chain lightning cannot affect the same target more than once.

==Notes==
* Chain lightning within the vicinity of neutral [[Ashlands Dvergr]] has the potential of damaging them, immediately turning them hostile.
